mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a high-inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market indicators are strong.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect reverses during high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong demand growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above 0.3% indicates a dual tightening of monetary policy and inflation persistence, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.3% and CPIAUCSL > 0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered months, or the effect reverses when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the effect reverses during high inflation or monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for five consecutive months signals a manufacturing recovery, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the effect is absent during demand weakness.
